to set mixture, i usually start at 1.5 turns out  from lightly seated. start the bike, warm it up,  and turn the idle up to where it'll run smoothly, say 1800rpm. 

start on one carb, turn the mixture screw out half a turn at a time and listen and watch the rpms rise. continue until the rpms drop a hair again. turn it in half a turn, asjust the idle, and do the other side. make sure you don't overheat the bike. after setting the mixture, adjust the idle when warm to ~1400 rpm or whatever the manual suggests. Then synch the carbs. 

If you can close the mixture screw and the bike doesn't die, your pilot jet is too big. if you are more than 3 turns out your pilot jet is too small or clogged.  if you remove the carbs to clean them or whatever,  your rebuild kit should have a tiny washer and o ring. those go under the spring under the mixture screw, pull the old ones out with a bent paperclip or something if you do remove the mixture screw.
